result.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
result.summary: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model. It preserves the chosen SDR base exactly and reconstructs HDR targets at an average PSNR of 43.03 dB across 400 images. On a benchmark of 100 sexual-content images, DRJanus evades detection by all six tested commercial moderation services and nine vision-language models. Across five agents, each evaluated on 120 task cases per threat setting, attack success ranges from 31.67% to 100% for moderation evasion and from 95% to 100% for task manipulation. We also explore cross-view consistency checks as a mitigation. These findings expose a gap in visual trust: securing what a machine reads does not secure what a user sees. A demo is available at https://qshen0629.github.io/DRJanus/

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DRJanus：利用 JPEG 的 HDR gain map 在单张图中嵌入两幅独立图像，使自动系统读到 SDR 基图、人眼在 HDR 显示下看到另一幅目标图，从而规避审核服务与 VLM，并操控多个智能体的任务行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「机器所见与用户所见不同」的可控双视图构造，可能为核查 VLM 内部状态究竟编码哪一路视觉证据提供刺激设计线索，跨视图一致性检查也可供思考视觉旁路与证据筛选的检测方式。
